newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to deal appropriately with excessive yen rise,dip.
newsitem.headline: MOF to deal appropriately with excessive yen rise,dip.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that the ministry would deal appropriately with an excessive rise or fall in the yen.
He also said it was unlikely there would be heated discussions over Japan's surplus at the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' summit meeting in Denver from June 20 to 22.
Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee meeting that Japan will explain to G7 members that it is going to steadily manage its economy centring on domestic demand.

"There is no doubt that stable (currency) rates support the macro-economy. Excessive weakness or strength in the yen is not desirable for the economy, so we would deal with that appropriately in that event," Mitsuzuka said.
He added that the Denver G7 summit meeting would confirm what the G7 nations had agreed to so far.
Mitsuzuka said Japan will explain at the summit meeting that it will pursue stable economic growth.
"I don't think opinions will clash over Japan's current account surplus (at the Denver G7 summit)," Mitsuzuka said.
He said that the Japanese economy was moving on to a solid growth trend and economic management centring on domestic demand would be established in the mid-term.
